description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of various configurations of the LaSQuE model compared to a baseline RoBERTa model without explanations, evaluated on a zero-shot classification task. The vertical axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 40% to 65% in increments of 5%. The horizontal axis lists six distinct model variants: “RoBERTa w/o Exp.” (light gray), “LaSQuE (mean)” (light blue), “LaSQuE” (orange), “LaSQuE (syn2real)” (green), “LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)” (purple), and “LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)” (dark gray, repeated label). The baseline RoBERTa model achieves approximately 46% accuracy. The LaSQuE variants show progressive improvements: “LaSQuE (mean)” reaches ~55%, “LaSQuE” (without specified variant) is at ~47%, “LaSQuE (syn2real)” is at ~47%, “LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)” reaches ~59%, and the final dark gray bar, also labeled “LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)”, attains the highest accuracy at ~62%. The chart visually demonstrates that incorporating synthetic-to-real adaptation and curriculum learning significantly boosts performance over both the baseline and simpler LaSQuE variants.
